title: Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalence, and Finite-Time Rigidity
summary: Classical spectral theory of reversible Markov chains characterizes the asymptotic relaxation dominated by the slowest eigenmode, governed by the spectral gap. This paper studies a complementary finite-time phenomenon: long before stationarity, many observables of the relaxation trajectory behave as if only a single spectral mode remains -- a collapse we term spectral purification. We develop a quantitative theory for it.
